def-cm15-asymptotic-data.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for preparation and cross-section measures, The physical reading of the scattering data of the page's restricted model class: the two-label central model of the central-model postulate, its reduced problem, the scattering motion of the relative coordinate on all of R, the energy and angular momentum carried by the motion, the asymptotic velocities, the impact parameter as an asymptotic perpendicular-distance limit, the polar advance and the deflection conventions, the adopted uniform-incident preparation and its flux and units, and the reading conventions (angles are relative-frame angles) together with the explicit exclusions and the status of the data as model data. The item fixes vocabulary and an adopted preparation model; it asserts no observation, no measured value, no law of nature and no counting of detected particles.

def-cm15-asymptotic-data:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the preparation and cross-section measures.

This item fixes the **scattering data** of the restricted model class of
[[post-cm05-central-model]] and the preparation conventions in which the
scattering statements of this page are phrased. All objects are model data;
nothing here is a measured value.

**(i) The scattering model.** A **central scattering model** is a model of
class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with $N=2$ labels, masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), no external forces, and a
static central pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])
whose collision-excluded interval satisfies $(0,\infty)\subseteq J_0$, so
that the only forbidden configuration is the collision $r=0$. Its **reduced
problem** is the one-label problem of class (ii) with reduced mass
$\mu:=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$ ([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\mu]=\mathsf M$) and the same
potential, presented through the relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$; by
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] the relative coordinate of every motion of
the model is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ and every pair of an
affine centre-of-mass motion and a solution of the reduced equation on a
common interval reconstructs a motion of the model.

**(ii) Scattering motions and their data.** Let $r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$
be a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$
with values $|r(t)|\in J_0$ and with constant angular momentum
$j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ for $J>0$ and an oriented orthonormal triad
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]],
[[lem-cm-oriented-orthonormal-triads]]). Call $r$ a **scattering motion** when it has a unique apsis $t_*$ with $\rho=|r|$ decreasing strictly before $t_*$, increasing strictly after it, $\rho(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$, and the nonzero limits below exist with the stated speed, equal finite impact-distance limits and finite equal half-advances. These are defining conditions, not deductions for arbitrary $C^2$ potentials. The finite-range theorem requires $u=0$ beyond some $R$, $E,J>0$, a simple outer turning point $V(r_*)=E$, $V'(r_*)<0$, $V(r)<E$ for $r>r_*$, and a trajectory staying above and attaining $r_*$. The repulsive Coulomb theorem instead requires $u=\kappa/\rho$, $\kappa,E,J>0$ and a trajectory attaining its turning radius. Each theorem proves the defining conditions in its own scope. Its **energy** is the constant
$$E:=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert r\rvert)>0$$
of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] (constant by
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4), its **asymptotic
velocities** are the limits
$$v_-:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}r'(t),\qquad v_+:=\lim_{t\to+\infty}r'(t),$$
taken in the sense of [[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]
(their existence under the hypotheses is a theorem, not a convention), and
its **scattering speed** is
$$v_\infty:=\lVert v_-\rVert_2=\lVert v_+\rVert_2=\sqrt{2E/\mu},$$
the equality being part of the scattering theorems. The **incoming branch**
is the trajectory restricted to times before its apsis. The **impact parameter** is the asymptotic perpendicular-distance limit
$$b:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_-\rVert_2}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2}=\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_+\rVert_2}{\lVert v_+\rVert_2}=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}>0.$$
Here the distance at each time is to the line through the origin in the limiting velocity direction, not to an exact affine trajectory line. For a finite-range potential, the sufficiently early incoming tail is a straight half-line whose affine extension has this distance; for Coulomb these are only limits, with no exact free tail or finite longitudinal intercept claimed. The dimension is $[b]=\ell$.

**(iii) Polar advance and deflection conventions.** Fix polar data
$(\rho,\theta)$ of the scattering motion in the triad, $r=\rho\,n(\theta)$,
$n(\varphi):=\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\varphi\,e_2$
([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]), and let $t_*$ be an apsis time,
$|r(t_*)|=\min_t|r(t)|$. The **polar advance of one half** is
$$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty),$$
defined by the limits asserted in the scattering theorems, and the
**polar advance of the motion** is $2\Delta$. The **scattering angle** is the
undirected angle between the asymptotic velocity directions,
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2\,\lVert v_+\rVert_2}\right)\in[0,\pi],$$
the incoming and outgoing velocity directions are oriented, so this is not the smaller unoriented angle between two lines;
the **signed velocity rotation** is the continuous rotation angle of
$r'(t)$, measured counterclockwise about $e_3$ relative to the incoming
direction, so that a positive value is a counterclockwise turn. The scattering
theorems give $\cos\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta)$ and the signed
rotation $2\Delta-\pi$; in particular, when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ the scattering
angle is
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi),$$
while for $\Delta\ge\pi/2$ the motion has wrapped past the backward direction
and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the wrapped value $\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$.
The **deflection map** at fixed model potential $u$, reduced mass $\mu$ and energy $E>0$ is the partial map $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)$ on those $b>0$ for which a scattering motion exists and all such motions have the same angle. Its corresponding angular momentum magnitude varies as
$$J(b)=\mu b v_\infty=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b.$$
Time translation and rotation of a motion do not change its angle. **Deflection branches** are $C^1$ branches of this partial map as defined in [[def-cm-scattering-data]].

**(iv) The uniform-incident preparation (adopted model datum).** The
**uniform-incident preparation** of a central scattering model with cutoff
$b_{\max}>0$ and flux $\Phi>0$ is the following adopted model of a scattering
experiment for the reduced problem: independent incident reduced labels with common energy $E>0$ and impact-azimuth probability measure
$$P(A)=\frac{\nu(A\cap D_{\max})}{\pi b_{\max}^2},\qquad D_{\max}=(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi).$$
Its density is $b/(\pi b_{\max}^2)$, and its total mass is one since $\nu(D_{\max})=\pi b_{\max}^2$. Angular momentum magnitude is $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$; its plane orientation may vary with azimuth. The **incident flux** $\Phi$ is the expected number of incident labels per unit area per unit time, with $[\Phi]=\ell^{-2}\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). The adopted total arrival rate is $\Phi\pi b_{\max}^2$, so for a Borel set $A\subseteq D_{\max}$ the expected incident rate is
$$\dot N(A)=\Phi\pi b_{\max}^2 P(A)=\Phi\nu(A).$$
Here $\nu$ is the incident area measure of [[def-cm-scattering-data]];
the rate of scattered
labels into a solid-angle set is the flux times the pushforward of $\nu$ under
the deflection map, whose density on a branch is the cross-section density
introduced in this page's cross-section definition. This is a predicted model
quantity: it reports no
detection, and its comparison with data requires a separately specified
experiment, apparatus model and statistical analysis.

**(v) Reading conventions.** All angles and lengths above are data of the
**relative** problem, equivalently of the centre-of-mass frame of the
two-label model: the relative coordinate $r$ and the centre of mass $X$ are
those of clause (i) and [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]. The
individual labels move along $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and
$x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ with $M=m_1+m_2$
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4), so their directions relative to
the centre of mass differ from $r$ by the mass factors and generally differ
from each other; an angle of the reduced problem is not, without further
computation, an angle of either label with respect to a laboratory frame.
"Target", "projectile" and "detector" are names for model components and
carry no empirical claim.

**(vi) Exclusions and status.** The class excludes velocity- or
time-dependent, non-central and non-potential forces; constraints and
reaction forces; collisions $r=0$; external forces; and models with more than
two labels, exactly as in [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (v). The
preparation of clause (iv) is one adopted idealisation among many; the
scattering theorems state separately which potentials, energies and angular
momenta produce the data of clauses (ii)-(iii). The quantities $\mu$, $u$
(with any parameters it carries), $E$, $J$, $b$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model
data; quantitative empirical use requires separately stated measured inputs
with uncertainties, and no statement of this page asserts that any physical
system is exactly a central scattering model or that any beam is exactly
uniform.

**Why the objects are defined.** The relative coordinate is a central-force
trajectory by the cited reduction theorem; the attached energy and angular
momentum are defined by [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] and are constant
on the trajectory by [[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4 and
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]]; the impact parameter is defined by its limiting distance, with existence and equality proved under the theorem-specific hypotheses; and the
preparation measure of clause (iv) is the measure $\nu$ of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. The arccosine of clause (iii) is defined because
the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives
$|\langle v_-,v_+\rangle|/(\lVert v_-\rVert_2\lVert v_+\rVert_2)\le1$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**Mathematical status.** The vocabulary is attached to the adopted model
class of [[post-cm05-central-model]]; the existence of the limits, the
identities for $v_\infty$, $b$, $\Delta$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$, and the
form of the deflection map under explicit potential hypotheses are the
content of the mathematics and physics theorems of this page, not of this
definition.

def-cm15-cross-section.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the Borel cross-section measures, The page's cross-section vocabulary for the uniform-incident preparation: the differential cross-section as the area-pushforward density of a deflection branch of a central scattering model, its units, the branch-sum convention, the truncated total cross-section over an angular window with finite or singular endpoints, and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading (adopted preparation, model rates not detections, finite samples, detector acceptance, no ideal total for a forward-divergent branch). The item defines model quantities; it asserts no observation, no measured value and no counting of detected particles.

def-cm15-cross-section:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Borel measures.

This item fixes the **cross-section** vocabulary of the central scattering
models of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] relative to the uniform-incident
preparation of that definition.

**(i) The differential cross-section of a branch.** Let a central scattering
model be given, let $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a **deflection branch**
in the sense of [[def-cm-scattering-data]] — an interval $(a_1,a_2)$ of
impact parameters with $\theta$ of class $C^1$ and $\theta'(b)\ne0$ — and
suppose the branch **records the deflection** of the model: for every
$b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of the model with impact parameter $b$,
fixed energy $E$ and angular momentum magnitude $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$ has scattering angle
$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\theta(b)$. Write
$(a_1,a_2)\ni b\mapsto\theta\in(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ for this bijection and
$b(\theta):=\theta^{-1}(\theta)$ for its inverse
([[def-cm-scattering-data]]). The **differential cross-section of the
branch** is the function
$$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta):=\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'\bigl(b(\theta)\bigr)\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2),$$
the cross-section density of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]. Its dimension is
$[\mathrm d\sigma/\mathrm d\Omega]=\ell^2$ (solid angle dimensionless in the
chosen convention, [[def-cm01-units]]), and one says "per steradian" for the
unit of solid angle.

**(ii) Branch sums.** If finitely many deflection branches of the same model
have pairwise disjoint image intervals $(\theta_1^{(j)},\theta_2^{(j)})$ that
do not overlap and each records the model's deflections on its interval, the
**differential cross-section of the model** on the union of the images is the
sum of the branch densities, and it is left undefined at angles belonging to
no branch image. No claim is made that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$ or
that the branch functions are reverse images of a single function.

**(iii) Cross-section measure and truncated totals.** For every Borel angular window $Y\subseteq(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
$$\sigma(Y):=\int_Y\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,d\lambda_1(\theta)=\int_{Y\times(0,2\pi)}b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|\,d\lambda_2.$$
These are integrals over measurable sets in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], with extended value $+\infty$ allowed. The measure-level identity of [[thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density]] identifies this with the area of the incident preimage. On a compact interior interval it equals the ordinary Riemann integral; on an open interval its value is the monotone limit over compact interior truncations, equivalently the nonnegative improper integral when finite. General Borel windows use the Lebesgue integral, not a two-piece interval improper integral.
The **ideal total cross-section** is the extended value $\sigma((\theta_1,\theta_2))$. If infinite, there is no finite ideal total. Every compact interior angular window has finite cross-section; more generally a cutoff whose incident preimage is bounded has finite cross-section. An arbitrary positive angular cutoff need not suffice for an arbitrary branch.

**(iv) The uniform-incident reading.** Under the uniform-incident preparation
of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv) with cutoff $b_{\max}$ and flux
$\Phi$, the model predicts the expected rate of scattered labels into an
angular window $Y$ to be the flux times its cutoff cross-section, for the portion of the branch fed by $b<b_{\max}$. Writing $T(b,\varphi)=(\theta(b),\varphi)$ on the branch rectangle and $D_{\max}=(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi)$, the cutoff measure is
$\sigma_{b_{\max}}(Y)=\nu(T^{-1}(Y\times(0,2\pi))\cap D_{\max})$,
and the rate is $\Phi\sigma_{b_{\max}}(Y)$; it equals $\Phi\sigma(Y)$ when the whole incident preimage lies below the cutoff. This is a prediction of the
model under the adopted preparation. In particular:

- $\sigma(Y)$ is **not** a probability per incident label, **not** a count of
  detected events, and **not** a property of any apparatus;
- a comparison with data requires a separately specified experiment: an
  apparatus model, a detector with finite angular resolution and acceptance,
  a sampling model and uncertainties, and a statistical analysis, none of
  which is supplied by this page;
- for a branch whose ideal total diverges at a forward angle, only windows of finite cross-section give finite model rates, and a finite measured rate constrains the model only
  jointly with the apparatus acceptance;
- finite samples fluctuate: an observed angular distribution can miss a
  branch's features with positive probability under ordinary sampling models,
  and agreement is evidence about the model-plus-apparatus assumptions, not a
  proof of the model.

**(v) Status and exclusions.** The branch hypothesis includes
$\theta'\ne0$: the definition excludes angles at which
$\theta'(b)=0$ (rainbow-type stationary deflections) and leaves them to
separate limiting measures. It also excludes, at the level of this page,
friction and tangential contact laws, attractive capture, screening,
radiation, relativistic and quantum modifications, and any identification of
the model parameters with measured electromagnetic quantities; those require
separate models or cross-framework items. The functions $\theta$, $b$ and the
data $E$, $J$, $u$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model data
([[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (vi)).

**Why the objects are defined.** The inverse $b$ is $C^1$ with
$b'(\theta)=1/\theta'(b(\theta))$ because a $C^1$ function on an interval with
nowhere vanishing derivative is strictly monotone and has a differentiable
inverse ([[def-cm-scattering-data]]); $\sin\theta>0$ on $(0,\pi)$; hence the
denominators do not vanish and the density is finite at every interior point
of the branch image. The pushforward identity that justifies the reading
"density carried by the branch" is
[[thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density]], a theorem of this page's
mathematical suppliers.

pthm-cm15-central-scattering.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the branch and preparation measures, The scattering prediction of the restricted two-label central model class with a finite-range $C^2$ potential and a simple outer turning point: the relative motion lives on all of time with one apsis and two monotone branches; the asymptotic velocities exist with speed $\sqrt{2E/\mu}$; beyond the range the branches are exactly free and the incoming and outgoing lines have perpendicular distance $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$; the half-angle advance is the stated quadrature and the asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle $\pi-2\Delta$ when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$; and on a smooth deflection branch that records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure has cross-section density $b|\mathrm db/\mathrm d\theta|/\sin\theta$ and the expected uniform-incident rate is the flux times the truncated cross-section. The result is a conditional deduction inside the adopted model class; it uses the model data $E,J,u$ and no measured value, asserts no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, and reports no detection.

pthm-cm15-central-scattering:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for clause 4 and its preparation measures.

Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, static
central pair potential $u\in C^2((0,\infty))$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $E>0$, $J>0$; write
$$V(r):=u(r)+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Suppose:

**(H1) finite range:** there is $R>0$ with $u(r)=0$ for every $r\ge R$;

**(H2) simple outer turning point:** there is $r_*>0$ with
$$V(r_*)=E,\qquad V'(r_*)<0,\qquad V(r)<E\quad(r>r_*).$$

Let $r:J_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model
on an interval $J_0$ with nonempty interior and with attached angular
momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ and attached energy $E$
([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]), and suppose
$|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for every $t\in J_0$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some
$t_*\in J_0$. Then:

1. **(The scattering motion.)** $r$ extends uniquely to a central-force
   trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ for $(\mu,u)$; the extension is
   the relative coordinate of a motion of the two-label model defined on all
   of $\mathbb R$, whose centre of mass is the affine extension of the
   original one. Along $\bar r$, $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies $\rho\ge r_*$,
   $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$ is strictly decreasing on
   $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on $[t_*,\infty)$; no collision
   occurs. Moreover the time quadrature
   $$\tau(r_0):=\int_{r_*}^{r_0}\frac{\mathrm ds}{\sqrt{(2/\mu)\bigl(E-V(s)\bigr)}}\qquad(r_0\ge r_*)$$
   is finite for every $r_0$ and satisfies $\rho(t_*\pm\tau(r_0))=r_0$.
2. **(Free asymptotes, speed and impact parameter.)** The limits
   $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\bar r'(t)$ exist and
   $$|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty .$$
   For every $t_1\ge t_*$ with $\rho(t_1)\ge R$ the motion is exactly free
   from $t_1$ on, $\bar r(t)=\bar r(t_1)+(t-t_1)v_+$ for all $t\ge t_1$;
   symmetrically for the incoming branch with $v_-$. The perpendicular
   distance from the force centre of the affine extensions of the incoming and outgoing free tails is the same number
   $$b=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}},\qquad\text{so that}\qquad J=\mu b\,v_\infty .$$
3. **(Polar advance and deflection.)** Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data of
   $r$ in an oriented orthonormal triad with $e_3=j/J$
   ([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]). Then
   $$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty) =\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{J\,\mathrm dr}{r^2\sqrt{2\mu\,\bigl(E-V(r)\bigr)}}$$
   is finite and positive, and the asymptotic directions satisfy
   $$\frac{v_+}{|v_+|}=-R_{2\Delta}\Bigl(\frac{v_-}{|v_-|}\Bigr),\qquad \frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{|v_-|\,|v_+|}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta),$$
   where $R_\alpha$ is the rotation of the plane
   $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)$ by $\alpha$. The scattering angle of the
   motion is $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$; if
   $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ then $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi)$ and the
   signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi$.
4. **(Cross-section of a deflection branch.)** Let
   $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a deflection branch of the model in the
   sense of [[def-cm15-cross-section]]: $\theta$ is $C^1$ with
   $\theta'(b)\ne0$, and for every $b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of
   the model with impact parameter $b$, fixed energy $E$ and angular momentum magnitude
   $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$ has scattering angle $\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)=\theta(b)$, with
   $0<\Delta(b)<\pi/2$. For each member of this family suppose (H2) and the trajectory hypotheses hold with its own $J(b)$ and turning point $r_*(b)$. Then, for every nonnegative Borel test function on the branch image, or real Borel test function absolutely integrable for its outgoing measure,
   $$\int_{(a_1,a_2)\times(0,2\pi)}g(\theta(b),\varphi)b\,d\lambda_2(b,\varphi)=\int_{(\theta_1,\theta_2)\times(0,2\pi)}g(\theta,\varphi)b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|\,d\lambda_2(\theta,\varphi),$$
   the outgoing angular measure of the branch has density
   $b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|$ with respect to $\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi$,
   and the differential cross-section of the branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta) =\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'(b(\theta))\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2).$$
   Under the uniform-incident preparation of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv), with cutoff $b_{\max}>a_1$ and flux $\Phi$, put $c=\min(a_2,b_{\max})$ and
   $$Y=\theta((a_1,c)),\qquad \sigma(Y)=\int_Y\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,d\lambda_1(\theta).$$
   The window uses the image of the open interval, with one-sided endpoint limits when necessary, and works for either monotonicity. The expected scattered rate from this branch portion is $\Phi\sigma(Y)=\Phi\pi(c^2-a_1^2)$, which is finite. Other branch portions, if present, have their own additive contributions.
5. **(Scope of the statement.)** The theorem asserts nothing about the
   deflection map outside the recorded branch: it neither asserts that
   $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}$ is decreasing, injective or free of
   stationary points, nor that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$; and it
   treats finite-range potentials only. The collisions, long-range
   potentials, velocity-dependent forces and external forces are excluded by
   the model class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] and by (H1).

pthm-cm15-rutherford-model.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for cross-section measures, the separate long-range Coulomb scattering theorem, as a model prediction: the repulsive $\kappa/r$ potential has a unique simple outer turning point and every relative motion of the stated data extends to all of time without collision, with asymptotic velocities of speed $\sqrt{2E/\mu}$ and asymptotic impact distance $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$; the deflection map is the $C^1$ decreasing bijection $2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$ with a single branch, the differential cross-section is the Rutherford density $(\kappa/4E)^2\csc^4(\theta/2)$, every angular band has the finite truncated cross-section $\pi(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2)$, and the ideal total cross-section diverges at forward angles. The parameter $\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model and is not identified with any electromagnetic quantity; the result reports no measurement, no screening law and no capture, radiation, relativistic or quantum modification.

pthm-cm15-rutherford-model:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the cross-section measures.

Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu$, and the **repulsive Coulomb
potential**
$$u(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}\qquad(r>0),\qquad \kappa>0,$$
where $\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model
([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\kappa]=\mathsf M\ell^3\tau^{-2}$), so that
$$V(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Let the data satisfy $E>0$, $J>0$ and put
$$b:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}}>0,\qquad \alpha:=\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}>0.$$
Then:

1. **(Turning data.)** $V$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, with
   $V(r)\to+\infty$ as $r\downarrow0$ and $V(r)\to0$ as $r\to\infty$; the
   equation $V(r)=E$ has exactly one solution $r_*>0$, it is simple
   ($V'(r_*)<0$), one has $V(r)<E$ for every $r>r_*$ and $V(r)>E$ for every
   $0<r<r_*$, and $V=U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J$ is of class $C^2$ with no other
   crossing of the level $E$.
2. **(Global non-colliding scattering motion.)** Let $r:J_0\to\mathbb R^3$
   be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model with attached angular
   momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3$ and energy $E$, with $|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for
   every $t\in J_0$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some $t_*\in J_0$. Then $r$
   extends uniquely to a central-force trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to
   \mathbb R^3$ whose extension is the relative coordinate of a motion of
   the two-label model on all of $\mathbb R$; $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies
   $\rho\ge r_*>0$ (no collision), $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$
   is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on
   $[t_*,\infty)$; the asymptotic velocities $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}
   \bar r'(t)$ exist with
   $|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty$, and the asymptotic perpendicular
   distance of each branch to its limiting direction equals
   $b=J/(\mu v_\infty)=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$, so that $J=\mu b\,v_\infty$. Unlike
   the finite-range case, there is no radius beyond which the motion is
   exactly free: the limits above are asymptotic.
3. **(Deflection and its single branch.)** With polar data $(\rho,\theta)$ in
   a triad with $e_3=j/J$, the half-angle of the motion is
   $$\Delta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr),$$
   its scattering angle is
   $$\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in(0,\pi),$$
   and its signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi=-2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$.
   For the family at fixed $\mu,\kappa,E$ and varying $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$, realised by the apsis initial data of [[thm-cm-coulomb-scattering]] clause 4, the **deflection map**
   $$\theta_{\mathrm{def}}:(0,\infty)\to(0,\pi),\qquad \theta_{\mathrm{def}}(b):=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb},$$
   is $C^1$ and strictly decreasing, hence a $C^1$ bijection with inverse
   $b(\theta)=\dfrac{\kappa}{2E}\cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}$; it is a single
   deflection branch of the model on $(0,\infty)$ with
   $\theta_{\mathrm{def}}'(b)\ne0$ everywhere and no wrapping
   ($0<\Delta<\pi/2$ for every $b>0$).
4. **(Cross-section, angular cutoffs and divergence.)** The differential
   cross-section of that branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)=\Bigl(\frac{\kappa}{4E}\Bigr)^2\csc^4\frac{\theta}{2}\qquad(0<\theta<\pi),$$
   finite and positive; for $0<\theta_1<\theta_2<\pi$ the truncated total
   cross-section over the angular band is the finite number
   $$\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\theta_2)\bigr) =\pi\bigl(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2\bigr),$$
   and by monotonicity the band $\theta\ge\theta_1$ has
   $\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\pi)\bigr)=\pi b(\theta_1)^2 =\pi\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{2E}\bigr)^2\cot^2\frac{\theta_1}{2}$; whereas the
   truncated integral over $(0,\theta_0)$ diverges for every
   $\theta_0\in(0,\pi)$, so the **model has no finite ideal total cross-section**. Every positive angular cutoff therefore yields a finite
   truncated cross-section, and the model is predictive only jointly with an
   angular acceptance.
5. **(Status of the parameter and exclusions.)** The coupling $\kappa$ is a
   parameter of the mechanical model. This item does not identify it with
   $q_1q_2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ or with any electromagnetic quantity, states
   no measured value, and asserts no screening law for a medium of
   scatterers. Attractive Coulomb scattering (for which capture is possible
   for suitable data), inelastic, radiative, relativistic and quantum
   modifications are outside the adopted model and this statement.

post-cm15-impulse.physical_scope: Adoption of the page's impact and open-mass extensions of the framework's force branch: an isolated reciprocal impulse at one time (a finite momentum jump of opposite sign for the two labels, with the regular dynamics retained away from that time), a collinear restitution contact law with coefficient $0\le e\le1$ fixing only the relative velocity, and an open-body material accounting for matter entering and leaving a body at given rates with given inertial velocities. The item adopts model extensions and names their mathematical renderings; it derives nothing from the smooth-force postulates, asserts no law of nature, no measured value for $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and excludes simultaneous contacts, friction, deformation modes and coefficients outside $[0,1]$.

post-cm15-impulse:
## Postulate

Adopt, as this page's **impact and open-mass extensions** of the force
branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the following three model extensions. Each is an adopted model, not a
consequence of the smooth-force postulates; each applies only where a
statement explicitly invokes it.

**(i) The isolated reciprocal impulse model.** A two-label force model with
masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), time window $I_0$,
configuration domain $Q$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]) and continuous
external-plus-pair force maps $F_1,F_2$ is **run in the isolated reciprocal
impulse model at $t_*\in I_0$** when there is a motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ of the associated first-order system
([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) such that:

1. $x_1,x_2$ are continuous on $I$ and twice continuously differentiable on
   each of $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$
   ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]],
   [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and
   $m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every $t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}$;
2. the one-sided limits
   $v_i^{\pm}:=\lim_{t\to t_*\pm}x_i'(t)$ exist in $\mathbb R^3$
   ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]);
3. there is a vector $J\in\mathbb R^3$, the **impulse**, with
   $$m_1\bigl(v_1^+-v_1^-\bigr)=J,\qquad m_2\bigl(v_2^+-v_2^-\bigr)=-J .$$

The two equations of clause 3 are the **reciprocal finite-jump form** of the
isolated impulse: the two labels receive equal and opposite momentum changes.
The model places no bound on the force maps across $t_*$; its distributional
rendering by test-function pairings is proved in
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]]. The dimension of the impulse
is $[J]=\mathsf M\ell\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(ii) The collinear restitution contact law.** A model run in the isolated
reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$ is **collinear** when there is a unit vector
$n\in\mathbb R^3$ (the **contact direction**) with $v_i^{\pm}\parallel n$ for
$i=1,2$ and $\langle v_2^--v_1^-,n\rangle<0$ (the labels approach along $n$).
For a collinear contact, adopt a **coefficient of restitution** $e\in[0,1]$ —
a dimensionless model datum of the pair and the contact — and the **restitution
law**
$$v_2^+-v_1^+=-e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
For $e=1$ the contact is called **elastic**, for $e=0$ **perfectly inelastic**
and otherwise **semi-elastic**; the law is a constitutive assumption, not a
consequence of the impulse equations of clause (i), and $e$ is not derived
from the masses or the approach speed. The law is stated only for a single
collinear contact; simultaneous contacts, repeated contacts and tangential
(friction) impulses are outside the model.

**(iii) The open-body material accounting.** Adopt for a body whose mass,
velocity, external force and exchanged matter are described by maps
$m:I\to(0,\infty)$, $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $F:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
$r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$ and
$w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ (mass rates and *inertial*
velocities of the matter entering and leaving, measured in the same inertial
frame as $v$) the **material balance identities**
$$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad (mv)'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}} .$$
They are the mathematical rendering of "gains $r_{\mathrm{in}}\,\mathrm dt$ of
matter with velocity $w_{\mathrm{in}}$, loses $r_{\mathrm{out}}\,\mathrm dt$
with velocity $w_{\mathrm{out}}$, and feels the external force $F$", and they
are adopted rather than derived from a closed-system law. Their product-rule
consequence $mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$
is proved in [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]; in particular the
closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ is recovered only when
$r_{\mathrm{in}}w_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}w_{\mathrm{out}}$.
The model parameters $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}},w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}$
are model data with $[r_{\mathrm{in}}]=[r_{\mathrm{out}}]=\mathsf M\tau^{-1}$
and $[w_{\mathrm{in}}]=[w_{\mathrm{out}}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$.

pthm-cm15-impact-balance.physical_scope: The conditional consequences of the page's adopted impact and open-mass extensions: total momentum is continuous across an isolated reciprocal impulse with the impulse removed from the second label; a smooth-force motion with continuous force maps cannot carry a nonzero impulse, so the contact model is an extension rather than a smooth-force theorem; a collinear contact with coefficient of restitution $e\in[0,1]$ has the stated post-impact velocities and kinetic-energy change, is dissipative for $e<1$, and its contact law is an independent assumption not derivable from momentum balance; and the open-body material accounting yields the derived law $mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$ with the rocket thrust as the special case. The result is a conditional deduction from adopted model data; it asserts no measured value of $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and identifies no observed dissipation mechanism.

pthm-cm15-impact-balance:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]),
inherited from the statement of
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]], whose distributional jump
lemma uses it; the algebraic clauses used here do not otherwise use choice.
Adopt the impact and open-mass extensions of [[post-cm15-impulse]], with
$m_1,m_2>0$, an interval $I$ with nonempty interior, $t_*\in I$, a motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ run in the isolated reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$
with impulse $J$ and one-sided velocities $v_i^\pm$, and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\qquad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\qquad P(t):=m_1x_1'(t)+m_2x_2'(t).$$
Then:

1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the
   impact,
   $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$
   and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$:
   $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$.
2. **(Smooth-force exclusion.)** Let $x$ be a motion of the smooth force
   branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and
   [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] on $I$ along which the force maps are
   continuous. Then the momentum curves $p_i=m_ix_i'$ are of class $C^1$ on
   $I$; in particular
   $$p_i(t_*^+)=p_i(t_*^-)\qquad(i=1,2),$$
   so $J=0$: no motion of that class carries a nonzero isolated impulse. The
   finite-jump model of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i) is therefore a
   genuine extension of the smooth-force branch, not one of its cases.
3. **(Collinear restitution solution.)** Suppose in addition that the
   contact is collinear with contact direction $n$ and coefficient of
   restitution $e\in[0,1]$ ([[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii)). Then
   $$J=\mu(1+e)\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),$$
   $J$ is parallel to $n$, the centre-of-mass velocity
   $V:=M^{-1}(m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-)$ is unchanged across the impact, and the
   post-impact velocities are
   $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
4. **(Kinetic energy of the impact.)** The kinetic-energy change across the
   impact is
   $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2} -\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2} =-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0,$$
   with equality if and only if $e=1$ or $v_2^-=v_1^-$. For $0\le e<1$ the
   contact model is dissipative: the total kinetic energy of the two labels
   is not conserved across the impact, and the deficit
   $\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ is a quantity of the
   adopted contact law. This item identifies it with no measured heat,
   temperature, sound or deformation observable.
5. **(Momentum balance alone does not determine the impact.)** In the
   collinear case with $d^-:=v_2^--v_1^-$ and $d_n:=\langle d^-,n\rangle<0$,
   the impulse equations of clause 1 alone leave the scalar impulse magnitude
   free: for every real $J_n$ with $J_n\le \mu d_n$ (so that the contact is
   separating or grazing) the velocities
   $$v_1^+=v_1^-+\frac{J_n}{m_1}n,\qquad v_2^+=v_2^--\frac{J_n}{m_2}n$$
   satisfy the reciprocal impulse equations with impulse $J=J_nn$ and
   preserve the total momentum, and their kinetic-energy change is
   $$\Delta K(J_n)=-J_n\,d_n+\frac{J_n^2}{2\mu},$$
   whose minimum over the admissible range is
   $\Delta K(\mu d_n)=-\frac{\mu}{2}d_n^2$ at the perfectly inelastic value
   $J_n=\mu d_n$ (that is, $e=0$). The value of
   $J_n$ is fixed only by the contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (ii), which selects $J_n=\mu(1+e)d_n$; in particular momentum balance
   alone does not determine the post-impact velocities.
6. **(Open-body and rocket laws.)** Under [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (iii), with $m:I\to(0,\infty)$, $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
   $F,r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\dots$ and
   $w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the material
   balance identities, one has on $I$
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr).$$
   In particular: (a) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ then
   $m\,v'=F$ and $(mv)'=F$; (b) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ and
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'>0$ (mass loss) then
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr)=F-m'\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr),$$
   so the **thrust** is $T:=r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$,
   and the closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ fails unless
   $w_{\mathrm{out}}=v$; (c) if $r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ and $w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$
   then $m\,v'=F-r_{\mathrm{in}}v$, so capturing matter at rest in the
   inertial frame decelerates the body while $(mv)'=F$ still holds.

pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance.physical_scope: The moving-control-region bookkeeping of the adopted smooth open-flow model: under the adopted material mass and momentum balances for every material subregion, a non-material control region has the stated mass and momentum rates with boundary speed $w$, the material and fixed special cases follow, and under an inlet/outlet split of the boundary the flux terms become the entering and leaving mass rates with flux-averaged inertial velocities, so that the lumped open body obeys the material accounting and rocket law adopted in the impulse postulate. The balances are adopted hypotheses of this item, not derivations from particle mechanics; the result asserts no constitutive law, no boundary condition, no measured value and no observational claim.

pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport and divergence theorems.
**Adopt the smooth open-flow model** with the following model data
([[def-cm-continuum-motion]], [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]],
[[post-cm01-worldlines]], [[def-cm01-units]]): a nonempty open interval $I$;
a material region $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ (bounded open with $C^1$ boundary);
a motion $\chi$ of $B$ on $I$ of class $C^2$ whose time slices are
diffeomorphisms with positive Jacobian onto their images; a density field
$\rho>0$ of class $C^1$ and a spatial velocity field $u$ (the velocity of
$\chi$); a stress field $\sigma$ of class $C^1$
([[def-cm-traction-and-stress]]); and a continuous body-force density $b$;
all fields defined on a neighbourhood of the swept region over a compact
subinterval $J_0$ with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$. Adopt as the model's
**material balances**: for every material subregion $B'\subseteq B$ (a
nonempty bounded open subset with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$ whose images
$\chi_t(B')$ are bounded $C^1$ domains,
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]) and every
$t\in J_0$,

$$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho\,\mathrm dx=0,\qquad \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho u\,\mathrm dx=\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(B')}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS,$$

with $\nu$ the outward unit normal and the surface integral that of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. These two balance
laws are **adopted model assumptions** of this item, in the sense of the
open-body accounting of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (iii); they are not
derived from the particle postulates. Then, for every second motion $\psi$ of
a material region $B'\subseteq B$ on $I$ (the **control motion**) with
control regions $C_t:=\psi_t(B')$ that are bounded $C^1$ domains for
$t\in J_0$, spatial velocity $w$, and outward unit normal $\nu$.
Require its closed sweep $\Sigma_C:=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline{B'})\}$ to lie in the common open field domain. Require also either that this sweep lie locally inside the current material region $\chi_t(B)$, where localization supplies the local mass and momentum equations, or that those same local equations $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ and $\rho D_tu=\rho b+g$ be explicitly adopted on a neighbourhood of the control sweep. The control motion need not coincide with $\chi$. Then:

1. **(Control-volume identities.)** For every $t\in J_0$,
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx =-\int_{\partial C_t}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS, \tag{CV1}$$
   and componentwise
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho u_i\,\mathrm dx =\int_{C_t}\rho b_i\,\mathrm dx+\Bigl(\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS\Bigr)_i -\int_{\partial C_t}\rho u_i\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\qquad(i=1,2,3). \tag{CV2}$$
2. **(Material and fixed special cases.)** If $\psi=\chi$ (the control region
   is material, $w=u$ on the boundary), the flux terms vanish and (CV1),
   (CV2) reduce to the adopted material balances; if $\psi$ is the constant
   motion ($w=0$, $C_t=C$ fixed), then
   $$m_C'=-\int_{\partial C}\rho\,u\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS,\qquad P_C'=\int_C\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS-\int_{\partial C}\rho u\,(u\cdot\nu)\,\mathrm dS$$
   with $m_C:=\int_C\rho$, $P_C:=\int_C\rho u$; the last term is the momentum
   flux through the fixed boundary, and the relation is the fixed-region
   steady-flow balance of the engineering treatment when the fields are
   steady and the region fixed.
3. **(Inlet/outlet decomposition and the open-body law.)** Suppose that for
   every $t\in J_0$ the boundary decomposes into finitely many $C^1$ pieces,
   among which $\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu<0$),
   $\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu>0$) and the zero-flux rest,
   and put
   $$r_{\mathrm{in}}:=-\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{out}}:=\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,$$
   $$w_{\mathrm{in}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{in}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho u\,\bigl(-(u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS,\qquad w_{\mathrm{out}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{out}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho u\,\bigl((u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS$$
   (the flux averages are used only where the corresponding rate is
   positive), and write
   $$m:=\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx>0,\qquad P:=\int_{C_t}\rho u\,\mathrm dx,\qquad F_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\int_{C_t}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS .$$
   Then the control-volume identities read
   $$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}},$$
   and the lumped body with mass $m$ and velocity $v:=P/m$ satisfies
   $$m\,v'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr),$$
   the derived law of [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]. In
   particular, a body that only loses mass ($r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$,
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'$) has thrust
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$, and a body
   whose boundary moves with the material ($w=u$; no flux) has
   $m'=0$ and $P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}$.
4. **(Status.)** The balances displayed before clause 1 are adopted component
   models of the open flow, exactly as clause (iii) of
   [[post-cm15-impulse]] adopts the lumped accounting; this item proves only
   the two stated deductions (localization followed by the control-volume
   identities, and the inlet/outlet reading). It asserts no constitutive law
   for $\rho$ or $\sigma$, no boundary condition, no incompressibility, no
   smoothness beyond the stated one, and no empirical claim; the fields,
   the control motion and the region are model data.

rem-cm15-model-boundaries.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the scattering measures and vocabulary, A scope remark recording which claims the page's scattering, impact and open-flow items make, which model assumptions they adopt, and which claims they deliberately do not make: no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, no counting or probability interpretation of the cross-section, no contact scattering as a smooth-potential theorem, no measured values or electromagnetic identification of the Coulomb parameter, no laboratory-frame statement without the boost, no attractive capture, screening, radiation, inelastic, relativistic or quantum modifications, and no constitutive or boundary law for the open flow. The remark adds no claim of its own beyond the qualifications it records.

ex-cm15-hard-sphere-reflection-check.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the scattering measures and vocabulary, A declared contact model of a reduced label of mass $\mu$ reflecting elastically from a fixed impenetrable sphere of radius $a$: the reflection rule reverses the normal velocity component and preserves the tangential component, so that speed and angular momentum are conserved across the contact; the example computes the branch $b=a\cos(\theta/2)$, the uniformly constant cross-section density $a^2/4$ and the truncated total $\pi a^2$, and records that this is a contact (impulse) model outside the $C^2$ finite-range hypothesis of the central-scattering theorem, so its finite total does not contradict the Coulomb forward divergence. The data are declared model data; the example reports no observation and no measured value.

ex-cm15-rutherford-cutoff-check.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the scattering measures and vocabulary, A numerical check of the repulsive-Coulomb model prediction on declared model data in SI units: reduced mass $2\times10^{-26}\,\mathrm{kg}$, energy $10^{-18}\,\mathrm{J}$, angular momentum $4\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$ and coupling $\kappa=4\times10^{-30}\,\mathrm{J\,m}$ give $v_\infty=10^4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $b=2\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{m}$, $\alpha=1$, scattering angle $\pi/2$ and density $4\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm{m^2}$; the angular band values $\pi(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2)$ and the small-angle growth $\approx(16\pi\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm{m^2})/\theta_1^2$ are checked. All numbers are declared model data fed into the model formulas; the example asserts no measurement, no uncertainty budget and no comparison with any experiment.

cex-cm15-deflection-need-not-decrease.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the scattering measures and vocabulary, The smooth finite-range model has zero deflection for every impact parameter beyond its range, so any globally defined deflection map is constant on this tail and cannot be strictly decreasing. The zero potential is a genuine smooth witness with unique deflection for every positive impact parameter. As a separate model comparison, the adopted attractive refracting shell of index 3/2 retains its strictly increasing deflection on 0<b<a and its declared grazing jump to zero; it is outside the smooth central-scattering class. All computations concern declared model data and report no observations.

ex-cm15-impact-check.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the adopted collinear impact model: masses $2$ and $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ with one-dimensional velocities $3$ and $-1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ along the contact direction, for coefficients of restitution $e=1,\frac12,0$; the example verifies total momentum continuity, the impulse $J=-9\,\mathrm{N\,s}$ at $e=\frac12$, the post-impact velocities, and the kinetic-energy changes $0,-9,-12\,\mathrm{J}$, all in SI units. Every number is declared model data substituted into the model formulas; the example reports no measurement and no empirical comparison.

cex-cm15-restitution-above-one-increases.physical_scope: A hypothetical extension of the adopted impact model, replacing only its restitution range by arbitrary real e; a refutation of the claim that every real coefficient of restitution is admissible in the adopted isolated-impact model: with the collinear restitution law and $e=2$ on declared data, the kinetic energy rises by $3\,\mathrm{J}$ across an impact while the configuration is instantaneously unchanged, so the total mechanical energy of a conservative two-label model is not conserved; values $e>1$ therefore signal an omitted internal energy reservoir and are excluded from the conservative contact model of this page, which restricts $e$ to $[0,1]$. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement.

cex-cm15-momentum-alone-does-not-fix-the.physical_scope: A refutation of the claim that the reciprocal impulse equations alone determine a collinear impact: with masses $2$ and $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ and incoming velocities $3$ and $-1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, both the sticking outcome and the elastic outcome satisfy the equal-and-opposite momentum jumps with impulses $-6\,\mathrm{N\,s}$ and $-12\,\mathrm{N\,s}$ respectively and total momentum $0$, while velocities and kinetic-energy changes differ. Hence the contact law fixing the impulse (or the coefficient of restitution) is an independent model datum. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement, no determination of any real coefficient and no observation.

ex-cm15-rocket-check.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the open-body material accounting: a body of initial mass $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ losing mass at $1\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}$ with no external force and ejecta of constant speed $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ relative to the body has velocity $v(t)=2\ln(3/(3-t))\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from rest, satisfies the material balance identities, and violates the naive closed-system law $(mv)'=F$; the example verifies the identities, the thrust $2\,\mathrm{N}$ and the failure of the naive law on declared model data. It reports no measurement, no engine data and no empirical comparison.

ex-cm15-control-volume-check.physical_scope: Two declared checks of the smooth open-flow bookkeeping: (i) the exact uniform-expansion model $\rho(t)=\rho_0e^{-3\alpha t}$, $u(t,x)=\alpha x$, $p=p_0-\rho\alpha^2\lvert x\rvert^2/2$, whose fields satisfy the adopted local balances and whose fixed-ball and material-ball control regions satisfy the mass and momentum rates of the moving-control-region theorem; (ii) an idealised steady elbow with declared inlet/outlet data, where the inlet/outlet split gives the mass flux $0.4\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}$ and the dynamic force $\lvert\dot m(v_{\mathrm{out}}-v_{\mathrm{in}})\rvert\approx3.578\,\mathrm{N}$ once the pressure part is declared negligible. Both are conditional computations on declared fields; the example reports no measurement and no solution of a boundary-value problem.
